messages:
alex: Heads-up — I'm about to land a tiny Terraform change that moves per-model feature flags out of the global ConfigMap and into per-model annotations + a sync-to-secret step. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/8123. @devon @maria can you sanity-check the rollout plan?

maria: Quick question: why annotations + secret instead of a CRD?

alex: Main reasons: 1) faster rollout with existing kustomize/helm overlays, 2) secrets give us per-replica immutability for sensitive toggles, 3) avoids operator churn for now. We can iterate to a CRD later.

devon: Make sure the TF change writes the checksum annotation so we can trigger pod restarts predictably. Also we should avoid changing mount paths.

alex: Yep added `redwood.com/flags-checksum` annotation on Deployment and StatefulSet templates. TF snippet in the PR:
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_deployment" "model" {
  metadata {
    annotations = {
      "redwood.com/flags-checksum" = sha256(file("${path.module}/flags/${var.model}.yaml"))
    }
  }
  # ...
}
```

jen: How will the sync-to-secret run? Is that a k8s controller or a CI job?

alex: It's a controller (sync-agent) that watches annotations and writes into a sealed secret store (we still use sealed-secrets for the bootstrap). The controller will run in each cluster; the TF change just wires ServiceAccount + RBAC.

sam: SRE concern: during rollout pods might see config change and restart — what's the canary strategy?

alex: Plan: 1) apply TF with controller + RBAC no-deploy (controller image disabled), 2) deploy controller to a single canary namespace, 3) label two models for canary (low-traffic), 4) flip controller to sync mode for those models, 5) observe 24h, then flip globally.

maria: Add a feature-flag gating in controller so we can opt out models by annotation like `redwood.com/flags-sync: "false"`.

alex: Good call — added that.

devon: Also document rollback: controller should not delete secrets if annotation removed unless `redwood.com/flags-delete: "true"`. Otherwise we risk data loss.

alex: Implemented safe-delete default = false.

jen: Anything for Terraform plan output we should watch for? I ran `tf plan` and it wants to update 42 resources — mostly deployment annotations and a couple RBAC roles.

alex: That's expected. The risky ones are RoleBindings in prod; I'll open a separate change request for a staged apply (prod RBAC after canary).

sam: Reminder: update the console dashboards to show where flags are sourced (ConfigMap vs Secret) so support doesn't get confused.

alex: Filed frontend ticket #INF-1794 to add a small badge on model pages.

maria: One more: kustomize overlays — ensure we don't accidentally patch the global configmap for older clusters. Maybe keep a compatibility path: if `redwood.com/flags-source` missing -> fall back to global ConfigMap.

alex: Controller will do that fallback. We'll also keep a migration script that copies existing keys into per-model files in the repo.

jen: Can you paste the kubectl commands we'll use during canary so SRE can run them manually if needed?

alex: Sure:
```
# label canary model
kubectl label ns model-foo redwood-canary=true
# watch rollout
kubectl rollout status deploy/model-foo-deployment -n model-foo
# verify secret exists
kubectl get secret model-foo-flags -n model-foo -o yaml
```

devon: Add a smoke-check: curl the /health endpoint and the flag toggles route to ensure runtime picks up new keys.

alex: Added smoke-check to PR description.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: planned apply scheduled for 2024-07-12T03:00:00Z (canary cluster). Subscribe with `deploy-bot subscribe infra` to get updates.

sam: LGTM from SRE if we keep staged RBAC and the canary labeling. :thumbsup:

maria: I'll review the TF and controller tests today. If anything odd, I'll @alex in the PR.

alex: Thanks all — merging the infra change after a green test run, won't flip controller to global without another ping here.

jen: Nice, thanks for writing the migration script too.

alex: np. will post a short runbook in #help once canary is healthy.
